mainTopic: רבי אליעזר's ban on taking a פרה אדומה and other קרבנות from non-Jews: the story of דמא בן נתינה, the worry about רביעה, and challenges from פסוקים
overview: רבי אליעזר holds that a פרה אדומה may not be bought from a non-Jew. The גמרא tests this against the story of דמא בן נתינה, who gave up a fortune rather than wake his father. In the end of that story the Sages buy a red heifer from him, and the גמרא answers that the purchase went through Jewish merchants. A ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר also worries that someone did רביעה with the animal. The גמרא then works out how far back the guarding had to go: from the heifer's conception, then from its mother's conception, but not as far as the grandmother. It also explains how they knew to guard the calf (a red cup during mating, and a herd known for red calves). Next, רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא report that רבי אליעזר disqualified all קרבנות from non-Jews. They answer the פסוק about the flocks of קדר by saying the nations will convert in the future, proven from צפניה, and the גמרא gives a second version of this discussion. Finally, the גמרא challenges the rule from משה's request to פרעה and from יתרו's offerings, answering that both were before מתן תורה, and begins a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: דמא gives up a fortune to honor his father
steps.stepSummary: The story of דמא בן נתינה ends: he passed up a profit of 600,000 (or 800,000 according to רב כהנא) because the keys were under his sleeping father's head.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a profit of six hundred thousand. רב כהנא teaches: eight hundred thousand. The keys were lying under his father's head, and he did not disturb him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the story it brought as a challenge to רבי אליעזר. The Sages wanted to buy stones for the אפוד from a non-Jew, and he refused to wake his father even for a fortune.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point that matters for the argument is that the Sages tried to buy holy stones from a non-Jew. The same word "ויקחו" appears for the משכן donations, so if buying from a non-Jew was allowed there, the word cannot be the source of רבי אליעזר's ban on buying a פרה אדומה from a non-Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches, meaning he has a different version of the story
The place by his head, his pillow

phrases.english: for six hundred thousand [dinars] profit,
phrases.notes: This picks up in the middle of the story of דמא בן נתינה. The Sages wanted to buy stones for the אפוד from him.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana teaches: for eight hundred thousand,
and the keys were lying
under his father's head,
and he did not disturb him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא שָׂכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun before this section, which was brought to challenge רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's derivation from "ויקחו" that a פרה אדומה may not be bought from a non-Jew
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word "ויקחו" is used for the משכן donations, yet the Sages tried to buy the אפוד stones from a non-Jew. So the word cannot ban buying from non-Jews.

steps.title: Onyx stones break off the list
steps.stepSummary: The words "אבני שהם" have no "and" before them, so they cut the stones off from "ויקחו לי".
steps.simpleTranslation: "Onyx stones" interrupted the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אליעזר. It says the stones of the אפוד are not included in "ויקחו", so buying them from a non-Jew proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most items in the משכן list begin with "and", which ties each one back to "ויקחו לי תרומה". "אבני שהם" starts with no "and", so it breaks the chain. The stones are not covered by the "take" rule, and the story about them is no proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Onyx stones, which were worn on the אפוד
Interrupted the topic, cutting it off from what came before
The apron-like garment of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: "Onyx stones" interrupted the matter,
phrases.notes: שמות 25:7. Unlike the items before them, these words have no "and" in front.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אַבְנֵי שֹׁהַם״ הִפְסִיק הָעִנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the אפוד stones story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: the verse's wording separates the stones from "ויקחו"
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stones are part of the "ויקחו" list, so buying them from a non-Jew would contradict רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The stones are cut off from "ויקחו", so the story does not touch רבי אליעזר's source.

steps.title: "And stones to be set" links back
steps.stepSummary: The very next words, "ואבני מלואים", start with "and", which ties the stones back into the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written "and stones to be set," which goes back and joins it in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The next phrase has an "and", so the stones are tied back to "ויקחו" after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer relied on a missing "and". But "ואבני מלואים" brings the "and" back and reconnects the list. If so, the stones are covered by "ויקחו" again, and the original challenge returns.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, used to open a challenge
Stones to be set, meaning the gems set in the חושן and אפוד
Went back and mixed it in, reconnecting it

phrases.english: But isn't it written "and stones to be set,"
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, שמות 25:7. Notice that this phrase does start with "and".

phrases.english: which goes back and joins it in!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא ״וְאַבְנֵי מִלּוּאִים״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that "אבני שהם" cuts the stones off from "ויקחו"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The following words "ואבני מלואים" bring back the "and", reconnecting the stones to "ויקחו".

steps.title: The פרה אדומה from דמא's herd
steps.stepSummary: A further challenge from the end of the same story: the Sages came to buy a פרה אדומה from דמא, a non-Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, the end of the story teaches: The next year a red heifer was born in his herd. The Sages of Israel came to him. He said to them: I know that if I asked you for all the money in the world, you would give it to me. Now I ask only for the money I lost because of my father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, stronger challenge. In this part of the story the Sages are buying a פרה אדומה itself from a non-Jew, which is exactly what רבי אליעזר forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first challenge needed a comparison through the word "ויקחו". This one needs no comparison, because the case is the very same subject, a פרה אדומה bought from a non-Jew. It goes straight against רבי אליעזר's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, which adds another challenge
The latter part of a teaching
Red heifer, used to purify people from contact with the dead

phrases.english: And furthermore, the latter part teaches:
The next year there was born to him
a red heifer in his herd,
the Sages of Israel came in to him.
He said to them: I know about you
that if I ask from you

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָמוֹן שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם אַתֶּם נוֹתְנִין לִי,
phrases.english: all the money in the world, you would give it to me;
now I ask from you only
that money which I lost because of my father.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, קָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge on top of step 3, taken from the end of the same story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that a פרה אדומה may not be bought from a non-Jew
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The story shows the Sages buying a פרה אדומה directly from a non-Jew.

steps.title: Bought through Jewish merchants
steps.stepSummary: In that story, the heifer was bought through Jewish merchants, so the Sages did not buy it from a non-Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, they bought it through Jewish merchants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the red heifer challenge. Jewish merchants bought the heifer from דמא, and the Sages then got it from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's rule concerns who the heifer is taken from for the holy purpose. Jewish merchants stood in the middle, so the Sages took it from Jews, not from a non-Jew. The story therefore does not contradict him.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's ban on buying a פרה אדומה from a non-Jew stands. In the story of דמא בן נתינה, the heifer passed through Jewish merchants first.
steps.confusionAlert: Read plainly, the story sounds like the Sages bought straight from דמא: they came to him and he named his price. The גמרא explains that Jewish merchants were the actual buyers, and the Sages acquired the heifer from them.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, עַל יְדֵי תַּגָּרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל זְבוּן.
phrases.english: There, they bought it through Jewish merchants.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, עַל יְדֵי תַּגָּרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל זְבוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the red heifer in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the purchase went through Jewish middlemen
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Sages bought the heifer directly from a non-Jew, against רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Jewish merchants bought it from דמא, and the Sages acquired it from Jews, so רבי אליעזר's rule holds.

steps.title: Isn't רבי אליעזר also worried about bestiality?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי אליעזר's only reason is the פסוק. It brings a ברייתא where he answers that the Jews guarded the heifer from birth, which shows he worries about רביעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is רבי אליעזר really not worried about רביעה? But a ברייתא teaches that the חכמים told him: 'There was a case where they bought the heifer from a non-Jew named דמא (some say רמץ).' He answered: 'Is that a proof? Jews were guarding it from the moment it was born!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רבי אליעזר's ban is only about the פסוק. It proves from a ברייתא that he is also worried someone committed רביעה with the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, his ban came from reading the פסוק about 'taking' the heifer. In the ברייתא, he brushes off the דמא story by saying Jews guarded the animal from birth. That answer only makes sense if his worry is what a non-Jew might have done to the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Bestiality: a person having relations with an animal. This makes the animal unfit for the מזבח.
He is concerned or worried about
Is that a proof? (rejects the evidence)

phrases.english: And is Rabbi Eliezer not concerned about bestiality?
But isn't it taught: They said to Rabbi Eliezer:
There was an incident, and they bought it from the non-Jew,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the פרה אדומה.

phrases.aramaic: וְדָמָא שְׁמוֹ, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רֶמֶץ שְׁמוֹ.
phrases.english: and Dama was his name; and some say Remetz was his name.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה?
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to them: Is there a proof from there?

phrases.aramaic: יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיוּ מְשַׁמְּרִין אוֹתָהּ מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁנּוֹלְדָה!
phrases.english: Jews were guarding it from the time that it was born!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא חָיֵישׁ לִרְבִיעָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from reading the פסוק to asking whether רבי אליעזר also has a practical worry.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that רבי אליעזר's ban comes only from the פסוק of 'taking'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His answer about guarding the animal from birth shows that he worries about רביעה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר holds both reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר has two separate requirements: buying from a Jew because of the פסוק, and the worry about רביעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds two things: the rule about 'taking', and he is also worried about רביעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. רבי אליעזר does not have just one reason; he has two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody has to choose between the פסוק and the worry. The פסוק requires buying from a Jew, and separately he worries about רביעה. That is why in the דמא story he answers with the guarding point.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Taking' or buying, the requirement learned from the פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds two things:
the 'taking', and he is also concerned about bestiality.
phrases.notes: 'Taking' points back to the פסוק from earlier, which requires the heifer to be bought from a Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר תַּרְתֵּי אִית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His reason is only the פסוק, so the worry about רביעה contradicts it.
steps.terutzMaskana: He holds both the פסוק requirement and the worry about רביעה.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר, a פרה אדומה needs two things: it must be bought from a Jew (the פסוק), and it must be free of any worry about רביעה.

steps.title: Guarding from birth isn't enough: what about the pregnant mother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests רבי אליעזר's line 'guarded from birth.' Someone could have committed רביעה with the mother while she was pregnant, and רבא teaches that the unborn calf would count as part of that.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'Jews guarded it from the time it was born.' But we should worry that someone committed רביעה with its mother while she was pregnant! As רבא said: the calf of a goring animal is forbidden, because she and her calf both gored; and the calf of an animal used for רביעה is forbidden, because she and her calf both had רביעה done to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's answer and points out a gap in it. Guarding from birth does not protect the calf from what happened while it was still inside its mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא teaches that an unborn calf counts as taking part in whatever is done to or by its mother. So רביעה with the pregnant mother makes the calf itself disqualified. Guarding only from birth leaves that time uncovered.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that gored, here one that killed a person
An animal that had רביעה done to it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיוּ מְשַׁמְּרִין אוֹתָהּ
phrases.english: The Master said: Jews were guarding it
from the time that it was born.

phrases.aramaic: וְנֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא רָבְעִי לְאִמַּהּ כִּי הֲוָה מְעַבְּרָה!
phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps they committed bestiality with its mother when she was pregnant!
As Rava said: The offspring of a goring animal is forbidden;
she and her offspring gored.
And the offspring of an animal used for bestiality is forbidden;
she and her offspring were used for bestiality.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא רָבְעִי לְאִמַּהּ כִּי הֲוָה מְעַבְּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the wording of רבי אליעזר's answer from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's statement that the heifer was guarded 'from the time it was born'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבא, רביעה with the pregnant mother counts against the calf. So guarding from birth is too late.

steps.title: Read it as 'guarded from conception'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording: the Jews guarded the heifer from the time it was formed, which covers the pregnancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: Jews were guarding it from the time it was formed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רבי אליעזר's line so that it covers the pregnancy as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the guarding started when the calf was formed in its mother, then the mother was watched during the whole pregnancy. That closes the gap that רבא's rule opened.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (reread the line this way)
When it was formed or conceived

phrases.english: Say: Jews were guarding it
from the time that it was formed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיוּ מְשַׁמְּרִין אוֹתָהּ מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁנּוֹצְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The guarding began only at birth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The guarding began when the calf was conceived, so the pregnancy is covered.
steps.confusionAlert: Only one word changes: שֶׁנּוֹלְדָה (born) becomes שֶׁנּוֹצְרָה (formed). The two look alike, so read carefully.

steps.title: What about the mother even before conception?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further. Maybe someone committed רביעה with the mother before she ever conceived. רבי אליעזר himself forbids the offspring of animals that are פסול for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that maybe they committed רביעה with the mother from the very start! As we learned in a משנה: all animals that are פסול for the מזבח, their offspring are allowed. And it was taught about this: רבי אליעזר forbids them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading. Even guarding from conception does not cover what was done to the mother earlier, and רבי אליעזר holds that the offspring of a disqualified animal is also disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows the offspring of animals that are פסול for the מזבח, but רבי אליעזר argues and forbids them. So by his own view, רביעה with the mother at any earlier time would disqualify the heifer. Guarding from conception is still not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, here meaning before the pregnancy
Animals unfit to be brought on the מזבח
And it was taught about it (a ברייתא commenting on the משנה)

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps they committed bestiality with its mother from the start!
As we learned: All those disqualified for the altar,
their offspring are permitted.
And it is taught about it: Rabbi Eliezer forbids.
phrases.notes: He means רבי אליעזר forbids the offspring too, even if they were conceived after the mother became disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא רַבְעוּהָ לְאִמַּהּ מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the corrected reading from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The corrected reading that guarding 'from the time it was formed' is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר holds that the offspring of a disqualified animal is also forbidden. So רביעה with the mother even before conception would disqualify the heifer, and guarding from conception cannot rule that out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי אליעזר's worry about רביעה reaches back past the heifer itself to its mother's whole history. The גמרא will need to answer how the דמא story could still work.

steps.title: The challenge depends on which version of רב נחמן we follow
steps.stepSummary: The worry about רביעה before conception is no problem according to רבא's version of רב נחמן, but it is a real problem according to רב הונא בר חיננא's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for רבא, who quotes רב נחמן: the argument is only about animals that had רביעה while they were consecrated, and if it happened while they were ordinary, everyone permits the offspring. But according to רב הונא בר חיננא, who quotes רב נחמן: the argument is about animals that had רביעה while they were ordinary, and if it happened while they were consecrated, everyone forbids the offspring. What can we say according to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the question from step 10. It shows that the question only works according to one of two versions of רב נחמן's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's version, רבי אליעזר forbids the offspring only if the רביעה happened after the mother was הקדש, so an earlier act does not matter. In רב הונא בר חיננא's version, רבי אליעזר forbids the offspring even if the רביעה happened while the mother was חולין. That would include a time before she conceived. So according to him, guarding 'from when it was formed' is still not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for this view, but not for another)
Consecrated animals, already set aside for the מזבח
What is there to say? (the challenge has no easy answer)

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions come from the same רב נחמן. רבא and רב הונא בר חיננא simply remember his words in opposite ways.

phrases.english: It works well according to רבא,
as רבא says in the name of רב נחמן:
The dispute is when the animals were subjected to רביעה
while they were consecrated,
but when they were non-sacred
everyone agrees they are permitted.
phrases.notes: 'They' here means the offspring, which may be brought on the מזבח.

phrases.english: But according to רב הונא בר חיננא,
who says that רב נחמן says:
The dispute is when they had רביעה while non-sacred,
but when they were consecrated
everyone agrees they are forbidden,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרָבָא, אֶלָּא לְרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the challenge of step 10 to one version of רב נחמן's teaching
steps.kashyaTarget: The גמרא's reworded reading (step 9) that the heifer was guarded from when it was formed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב הונא בר חיננא, רביעה with the mother even while she was חולין and before conception would make the offspring פסול, and guarding from conception does not rule that out.

steps.title: The Jews guarded the mother from when she was formed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording again: the Jews guarded the heifer's mother from the time the mother herself was formed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: the Jews were guarding it, meaning its mother, from the time she was formed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by moving the guarding back one generation, to the mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mother was watched from her own conception, no one could have done רביעה with her at any time. That closes the gap even according to רב הונא בר חיננא.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (the גמרא rereads a statement)

phrases.english: Say instead:
The Jews were guarding it,
meaning its mother, from the time she was formed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיוּ מְשַׁמְּרִין אוֹתָהּ לְאִמָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The guarding began only with the heifer itself, so the mother might have had רביעה before she conceived.
steps.terutzMaskana: The guarding began with the mother from her own formation, so no רביעה could have happened to her.

steps.title: What about the grandmother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether we should also worry that someone did רביעה with the heifer's grandmother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us worry that maybe someone did רביעה with the mother's mother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the same worry back one more generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רביעה with the mother can make her offspring פסול, the same logic seems to apply to the grandmother. That would make the mother פסול, and the heifer too. The worry could go back forever.

phrases.english: And let us worry that perhaps
someone did רביעה with her mother's mother!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵיחוּשׁ דִּילְמָא רַבְעוּהָ לְאִמָּא דְּאִמַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 12 by going back another generation
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that guarding the mother is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same worry that applied to the mother should apply to the grandmother.

steps.title: We do not worry that far back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we do not worry about such a distant possibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are not worried to such an extent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops the chain and says the worry does not go back to the grandmother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Guarding the mother is enough. A possibility two generations back is too far to concern us, so רבי אליעזר's statement stands.

keyTerms.meaning: So much, to such an extent

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's worry about רביעה reaches the heifer and its mother, but not the grandmother. The גמרא says 'we don't worry that far.'

phrases.english: We are not concerned to such an extent.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלֵּי הַאי לָא חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting how far the worry goes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry about רביעה goes back to every earlier generation.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not worry about a distant possibility like the grandmother.

steps.title: How did they know which calf to guard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's line about guarding from formation and asks how they knew in advance that this calf would be a red heifer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: The Jews were guarding it from the time it was formed. How did we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the line 'guarded from when it was formed' and asks a practical question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before a calf is born, nobody can see that it is red. So how could the Jews know that this one needed to be guarded from the start?

phrases.english: The Master said:
The Jews were guarding it
from the time it was formed.
How did we know?
phrases.notes: He means: how did they know ahead of time that this calf would come out red?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיוּ מְשַׁמְּרִין אוֹתָהּ מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁנּוֹצְרָה. מְנָא יָדְעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the reworded statement of step 9 with a practical question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the Jews knew before birth that the calf would be a red heifer worth guarding

steps.title: רב כהנא: a red cup during mating
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that they passed a red cup in front of the mother while the male mounted her, which would make the calf red.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: They would pass a red cup in front of her while the male mounted her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the question: they did something during mating that would make the calf come out red.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since they acted on purpose to produce a red calf, they knew from the moment of conception that this calf might be a פרה אדומה. So they could guard it from the very start.

keyTerms.meaning: They pass in front of her

steps.whatToRemember: The Jews could guard the heifer from conception because they planned for it to be red, using a red cup at the time of mating.

phrases.english: רב כהנא says:
They pass a red cup in front of her
at the time the male mounts her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: כּוֹס אָדוֹם מַעֲבִירִין לְפָנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They passed a red cup before the mother during mating so the calf would be red, so they knew from conception to guard it.

steps.title: If it is so easy, why is it so expensive?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if a red cup can make a calf red, why does a פרה אדומה cost so much?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why is its price so expensive?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא's red cup method. If it is that easy to make a red calf, a פרה אדומה should not be rare or costly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knew a פרה אדומה sold for a very high price. That high price suggests it is hard to get one. So the easy method from Step 16 seems to clash with what we know.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true

phrases.english: If so,
why is its price expensive?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the red cup method of Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's explanation that a red cup makes the calf red.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If red calves are easy to produce, the known high price of a פרה אדומה makes no sense.

steps.title: Two hairs can ruin it
steps.stepSummary: The price stays high because just two hairs of another color make the heifer פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since two hairs disqualify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the cup trick can make a calf mostly red, but even two hairs of a different color ruin it. So a fully kosher one is still rare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method helps, but it is not reliable enough to give a perfect result. A פרה אדומה must be completely red, so very few calves qualify, and the price stays high.

phrases.english: Since two hairs disqualify it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וּשְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת פּוֹסְלוֹת בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the method: it helps but does not guarantee a perfect result.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The red cup method makes producing a פרה אדומה easy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The method is not reliable, since even two off-color hairs disqualify the heifer, so it stays rare and costly.

steps.title: Why use the gentile's cows?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Jews bought from a gentile instead of using the cup trick on their own cows.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about theirs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks another question. If the trick could work on any cow, why did they need a gentile's herd at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's worry about buying from gentiles was רביעה. If the Jews could make a red calf with their own cows, they could have avoided that worry completely. So why did they choose this gentile's cows?

phrases.english: And what is different about theirs?
phrases.notes: Theirs means the gentile's cows. Why not just do the trick with a Jewish cow?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא דִּידְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the red cup account.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story that the heifer was bought from a gentile, together with the red cup method.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If any cow could be used, buying from a gentile seems unnecessary.

steps.title: His herd was known for red calves
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the gentile's herd had a track record of producing red heifers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: It was a herd that was known for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא explains that this gentile's cows were known to give birth to red calves. So it made sense to use the cup trick on one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trick alone is not reliable, as Step 18 showed. Combining it with a herd that already tends to produce red calves gives the best chance of a perfect פרה אדומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Known, having an established track record

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
With one that was known.
phrases.notes: He means the gentile's herd was known to produce red heifers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: בְּמוּחְזֶקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 and closes the red heifer discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a fact about the case: the herd had a known history.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was no reason to prefer the gentile's cows.
steps.terutzMaskana: His herd was known for red calves, so it was the best place to try the method.
steps.whatToRemember: The cup trick helps but is not enough on its own. That is why a פרה אדומה stayed expensive, and why they used a herd known for red calves.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר disqualifies all offerings from gentiles
steps.stepSummary: While sitting on a porch, one of the two אמוראים quotes that רבי אליעזר disqualified every קרבן bought from gentiles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא were sitting on the porch of רבי יצחק נפחא. One of them began and said: And so too רבי אליעזר would disqualify all the offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: A new scene starts. One of the two אמוראים quotes that רבי אליעזר applied his worry about gentiles to every קרבן, not only to the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וכן, 'and so too', ties this to the פרה אדומה discussion. Just as רבי אליעזר worried about רביעה with a gentile's heifer, he worried about it with any animal bought from a gentile for a קרבן.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha were sitting
on the porch of Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha.
One of them began and said:
And so too, Rabbi Eliezer would disqualify
in all the offerings, every one of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּתַח חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ וַאֲמַר: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פּוֹסֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion that extends רבי אליעזר's view from the פרה אדומה to all offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר disqualified all קרבנות bought from gentiles because of the worry about רביעה.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new reason. It is the same worry about רביעה that he had for the פרה אדומה, now applied to every קרבן.

steps.title: The colleagues challenge from קדר's flocks
steps.stepSummary: The second אמורא quotes how רבי אליעזר's colleagues challenged him with a פסוק about the nations' flocks being offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other one began and said: What did his colleagues answer רבי אליעזר? 'All the flocks of קדר shall be gathered to you'!
steps.whatsHappening: The other אמורא quotes the challenge that רבי אליעזר's colleagues raised. ישעיהו says the flocks of the nations will be brought and accepted on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes animals from non-Jewish nations, קדר and נביות, being offered and accepted. If offerings from gentiles will be accepted, how can רבי אליעזר say they are always פסול?

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish nation, descendants of ישמעאל

phrases.english: The other one of them began and said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אוֹתִיבוּ לֵיהּ חַבְרוֹהִי לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר?
phrases.english: What did his colleagues challenge Rabbi Eliezer with?
"All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered to you, etc."!
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 60:7. The rest of the פסוק says they will be accepted on the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אוֹתִיבוּ לֵיהּ חַבְרוֹהִי לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's rule that all קרבנות from gentiles are פסול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says flocks from the nations will be accepted on the מזבח, so offerings from gentiles cannot be automatically פסול.

steps.title: In the future they will all be converts
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that the nations in that פסוק will have become converts by then.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to them: In the future, they will all be converts who joined on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers that the פסוק speaks about the future, when all those nations will have converted. As converts, they are no longer suspected of רביעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His rule is about animals from gentiles today. The פסוק speaks about a time when the owners will be גרים, so their animals are not under suspicion. That means the פסוק does not contradict his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Converts who join on their own, often for personal gain
In the future, in the time to come

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to them:
They will all be self-made converts
in the time to come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: כּוּלָּם גֵּרִים גְּרוּרִים הֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the פסוק as speaking about a future time when the owners are converts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק shows that offerings from gentiles are accepted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק speaks of a future time when the nations will be converts, so their animals are not suspected.

steps.title: רב יוסף's פסוק that the nations will convert
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks where we see that the nations will convert, and brings a פסוק from צפניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is the פסוק? 'For then I will turn to the peoples a clear language.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a source for רבי אליעזר's claim that the nations will convert in the future. He quotes צפניה, which says the nations will all call in ה׳'s name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's answer depends on the idea that all the nations will convert. רב יוסף shows that this idea is in a פסוק‎: ה׳ will give the nations a clear language so they all serve Him.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק, what is the source?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: What is the verse?
"For then I will turn to the peoples
phrases.notes: צפניה 3:9

phrases.english: a clear language, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides a source for רבי אליעזר's answer in Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's claim that all nations will convert in the future.
steps.raayaSupportSource: צפניה 3:9, which says the nations will call in ה׳'s name with one clear language.

steps.title: Maybe they only leave עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges that the פסוק may only mean the nations will give up idols, not that they fully convert.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But perhaps it is from עבודה זרה that they turn away?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions רב יוסף's proof. Maybe the פסוק only means the nations will stop worshipping idols, while still doing other sins like רביעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling in ה׳'s name could just mean leaving עבודה זרה. That would not make them full גרים, so the worry about רביעה would remain. The proof would then not support רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: That they turned back from, withdrew from

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But perhaps it is from idol worship
that they turn away?
phrases.notes: He means only from idols, but not from other sins like רביעה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְדִלְמָא מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הוּא דַּהֲדוּר בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof of Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reading of the פסוק in צפניה as full conversion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק may only mean the nations give up idol worship, which would not remove the worry about רביעה.

steps.title: Serving Him together means full acceptance
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers from the end of the פסוק: 'to serve Him with one shoulder' means full service of ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: It is written, 'to serve Him with one shoulder.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף points to the end of the same פסוק. It says the nations will serve ה׳ together, which means keeping all of His מצוות, not only leaving idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Serving ה׳ 'with one shoulder' means the nations join fully, like everyone carrying the same load. That is full conversion, so they would not be suspected of רביעה. This supports רבי אליעזר's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: One shoulder, meaning together and fully

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
"To serve Him with one shoulder" is written.
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק in צפניה. It shows they will take on all of ה׳'s service.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: לְעׇבְדוֹ שְׁכֶם אֶחָד כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the end of the same פסוק to show full acceptance of ה׳'s service.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The nations might only stop worshipping idols.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'To serve Him with one shoulder' shows they will fully accept all the מצוות, so they will be true converts.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר disqualifies קרבנות bought from gentiles. The פסוק about the nations' flocks speaks of the future, when they will all be full converts, as צפניה says: 'to serve Him with one shoulder.'

steps.title: רב זביד's version: both אמוראים report רבי אליעזר's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that רב פפא taught the earlier discussion the way we learned it, but רב זביד taught it differently. In his version both אמוראים say that רבי אליעזר disqualified all offerings from גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא teaches it this way, and רב זביד teaches it this way: both of them say that רבי אליעזר would similarly disqualify all offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving a second version of the discussion we just learned. In this version, both אמוראים say the same things instead of each saying a different part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, one אמורא reported רבי אליעזר's ruling and the other reported his colleagues' challenge. In רב זביד's version, both of them report the ruling about all offerings. The content stays the same, but who said what changes.

keyTerms.meaning: teaches (passes on the text of a discussion)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same discussion in a different version, and only who said what has changed.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa teaches it this way,
and Rav Zevid teaches it this way:
both of them say:
phrases.notes: "Both" means רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא.

phrases.english: and similarly, Rabbi Eliezer would
disqualify all offerings (taken from gentiles).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא מַתְנֵי הָכִי, וְרַב זְבִיד מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the discussion covered in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both אמוראים report that רבי אליעזר disqualified all offerings from גוים.

steps.title: Both report the colleagues' challenge from the פסוק of צאן קדר
steps.stepSummary: In this version, both אמוראים also report that רבי אליעזר's colleagues challenged him with a פסוק. The פסוק says the flocks of קדר will be gathered and offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both say: what did his colleagues answer back to רבי אליעזר? "All the flocks of קדר will be gathered to you."
steps.whatsHappening: The colleagues challenge רבי אליעזר with a פסוק that seems to show the nations' animals will be offered on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדר is a non-Jewish nation. If its flocks will be accepted on the מזבח, that seems to go against רבי אליעזר's rule that offerings from גוים are not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: the flocks of קדר, a non-Jewish nation

phrases.english: And both say:
And what did they challenge him with,
his colleagues, against Rabbi Eliezer?
"All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered to you, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 60:7. The rest of the פסוק says they will come up with favor on My מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי אוֹתִיבוּ לֵיהּ חַבְרוֹהִי לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that offerings from גוים are disqualified
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says the flocks of a gentile nation will be accepted on the מזבח.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: in the future they will all be converts
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that in the future all the nations will be converts. So the פסוק is not talking about offerings from גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: in the future to come, they will all be converts who join on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends his rule. The people in the פסוק will no longer be גוים by then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about the future. By that time the nations will have become גרים, so their animals count as Jewish offerings. His rule against offerings from גוים is not affected.

keyTerms.meaning: "dragged-along" converts, people who join the Jewish people on their own

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
they will all be dragged-along converts
in the future to come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: כּוּלָּם גֵּרִים גְּרוּרִים הֵם לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the colleagues' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes who the פסוק is talking about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק talks about offerings from גוים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק talks about future converts, who are no longer גוים.

steps.title: The source that the nations will convert
steps.stepSummary: In this version, the source from צפניה is part of the reported teaching itself, continuing רבי אליעזר's answer. It shows that the nations will convert in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the פסוק? "For then I will turn to the peoples a clear language, so they all call in the name of ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The reported teaching continues with the source for רבי אליעזר's claim: a פסוק that says all the nations will call in the name of ה׳. Here the פסוק is part of the reported teaching, not something רב יוסף adds, as he did in the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's answer depends on the claim that the nations will convert. This פסוק is brought as proof that in the future they will all turn to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the פסוק (that proves this)?

phrases.english: And what is the verse?
"For then I will turn to the peoples
a clear language,
so that they all call in the name of the Lord."
phrases.notes: צפניה 3:9

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי קְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the nations will convert in the future

steps.title: רב יוסף: maybe they only give up idols
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges the proof. Maybe the פסוק only means the nations will stop serving idols, without actually converting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: but maybe it is only from עבודה זרה that they turn away?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף questions whether the פסוק really proves the nations will fully convert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling in ה׳'s name might only mean dropping עבודה זרה. If that is all it means, they would still be גוים, and the proof would fall apart. In this version רב יוסף asks the question, while in the first version אביי asked it.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the switch: in the earlier version אביי challenged and רב יוסף answered. Here it is the other way around.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects to it:
But perhaps it is from idol worship
that they turn away?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: וְדִלְמָא מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הוּא דְּהָדְרִי בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from צפניה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the פסוק as proof of full conversion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק might only mean the nations leave idol worship, not that they convert.

steps.title: אביי: "to serve Him" means full service
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers from the end of the פסוק, which says "to serve Him with one shoulder." That means full service of ה׳, which is conversion.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: it is written, "to serve Him with one shoulder."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the proof. The פסוק goes further than just leaving idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving up idols alone would not be called "serving Him." Serving ה׳ together, as one, means fully joining His service. So the nations will truly convert. Here אביי answers, while in the first version רב יוסף gave this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: one shoulder, meaning all together as one

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions the conclusion is the same: in the future the nations will truly convert. That is why the פסוק about their flocks does not go against רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
"To serve Him with one shoulder" is written.
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק in צפניה 3:9.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לְעׇבְדוֹ שְׁכֶם אֶחָד כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the rest of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The nations only give up עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They fully serve ה׳, which means they convert.

steps.title: Challenge from משה asking פרעה for offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule against offerings from גוים. משה asked פרעה, a non-Jew, to give the Jews animals for offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: "And משה said: you too shall give into our hands offerings and burnt-offerings."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new set of challenges to the idea that animals from גוים cannot be used as offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה asked פרעה himself to supply animals for קרבנות. That suggests animals from a גוי can be offered.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"And Moses said: You too
shall give into our hands offerings and burnt-offerings!"
phrases.notes: שמות 10:25

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה גַּם אַתָּה תִּתֵּן בְּיָדֵנוּ זְבָחִים וְעֹלֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line of challenges to the rule itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that offerings may not be taken from גוים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה asked a גוי to supply animals for offerings.

steps.title: Before מתן תורה it was different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that משה's request was before מתן תורה, when this rule did not yet apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before the giving of the Torah it was different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to when it happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against offerings from גוים only started once the Torah was given. משה spoke to פרעה in מצרים, before הר סיני, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: before the giving of the Torah

phrases.english: Before the giving of the Torah it is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from משה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה's request shows that offerings from גוים are allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Before מתן תורה the rule did not apply yet.

steps.title: Challenge from יתרו's offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another challenge: יתרו, who was not Jewish, brought offerings to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "And יתרו, משה's father-in-law, took a burnt-offering and offerings for God."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק that seems to show offerings from a non-Jew being brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יתרו was a non-Jew, yet he brought קרבנות to ה׳. This challenges the rule again, this time from a story that happened in the מדבר.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And Yitro, Moses' father-in-law, took
a burnt-offering and offerings for God!"
phrases.notes: שמות 18:12

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וַיִּקַּח יִתְרוֹ חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה עֹלָה וּזְבָחִים לֵאלֹהִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that offerings may not be taken from גוים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יתרו, a non-Jew, brought offerings to ה׳.

steps.title: יתרו also came before מתן תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer as before: יתרו's offerings were also brought before מתן תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: יתרו was also before the giving of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same time-based answer for the story of יתרו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יתרו came and brought his offerings before מתן תורה, then the rule did not apply yet. So his offerings do not go against it.

phrases.aramaic: יִתְרוֹ נָמֵי קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הֲוָה.
phrases.english: Yitro was also before the giving of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִתְרוֹ נָמֵי קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the יתרו challenge using the same idea as step 34.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יתרו's offerings show that offerings from גוים are allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: יתרו came before מתן תורה, so the rule did not apply yet.

steps.title: But what about the opinion that יתרו came after מתן תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this answer only works for the opinion that יתרו came before מתן תורה. It begins to ask about the opinion that he came after.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says יתרו came before מתן תורה. But according to the one who says…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. The answer about timing may not work for everyone, and the question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an argument about when יתרו arrived. For the opinion that he came after מתן תורה, the answer "it was before the Torah" no longer works, so the challenge comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: according to the one who says

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says:
Yitro was before the giving of the Torah.
But according to the one who says:
phrases.notes: The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: יִתְרוֹ קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הֲוָה, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the answer in step 36 works for every opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that יתרו came before מתן תורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the opinion that יתרו came after מתן תורה, the timing answer does not work.
